pr_body:
This re-introduce the full hash and compre functions for Address,
which was reverted https://github.com/systemd/systemd/commit/1d30fc5cb64ecba2f03fe42aa0d8c65c3decad82 (https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/17851).

The issue https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/17831, which is fixed by https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/17851, is handled in a different way;
simply ignore to configure the conflicted DHCPv6 address. Previously, we
warn about the conflict, but continue to configure the address anyway, and
the kernel ignores the request. So, it is not necessary to request the
conflicted address in networkd side.

This fixes the following issues:
- when a link has an address, and corresponding .network file has the
  address with different prefix length, then the prefix length specified
  in the .network file will not be applied,
- we cannot specify multiple IPv4 addresses with different prefix
  length, e.g.
  ```
  Address=10.10.10.10/24
  Address=10.10.10.10/16
  ```
  This is spurious setup, but the kernel allows it.

Fixes https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/22515.

issue_context.title: `networkctl reload` did not apply new prefix length for address
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
 > v249.4

**Used distribution**
 > CentOS 8 stream

**Linux kernel version used** (`uname -a`)
> `5.6.13` with patches

I have a config that looks like this:
```
$ cat /etc/systemd/network/1-fb_networkd-eth0.network 
[Match]
MACAddress = 48:57:DD:05:C8:DC
Name = eth0

[Network]
Address = <primary address>/64
IPv4LLRoute = true
IPv6AcceptRA = true

[IPv6AcceptRA]
UseMTU = false
UseAutonomousPrefix = false
UseOnLinkPrefix = false
DHCPv6Client = false
```

I apply the config with `networkctl reload && networkctl reconfigure eth0` and `ip addr` shows the expected address with prefix length 64.

But if I change the line in the config from `Address = <primary address>/64` to `Address = <primary address>/128` (i.e. only the prefix length has changed), and do `networkctl reload` and `networkctl reconfigure eth0`, the address and prefix length as shown by `ip addr` is not updated. The only way I successfully got the new prefix length to apply is if I do `networkctl down eth0 && networkctl up eth0`. Is this expected?
comments:
Yeah, I know the issue...

Previously, once I changed the hash function for addresses to takes into account prefix length of address, but it causes an issue (though I forgot the detail...). So, now the function hashes only address. I will re-investigate the previous issue and this later.

Note, the issue should be occurs only on IPv6, as the prefix length of IPv4 addresses is already managed by the hash function.
Thanks @yuwata ! Your PR worked like a charm
